articleTitle: Brain Tumor Classification Based on Federated Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Optimization and Applications (ICOA)
abstract: This paper investigates the challenges of brain tumor classification and focuses on diagnostic performance while preserving the patient's privacy by investigating decentralized using federated learning. Brain tumor are considered one of the significant health risks and a widespread cancer disease, and the more accurate classification methods will help to diagnose the disease and for effective treatment planning. Conventional methods encounter many difficulties because of the limited availability of diverse medical imaging data as well as privacy regulations. To address these challenges, this method allows for decentralised training across multiple data centres by using the Federated Learning method. The proposed method utilises a pre-trained DenseNet model within an FL environment. This approach guarantees effective feature selection, improving the overall performance of the classification model. The training data remains localised at each node, and only the trainable weights and model updates are shared, therefore preserving data confidentiality. The FL model collects these updates to build a model that is capable of classifying MRI images. The study assesses the efficacy of the FL model through the utilisation of three publicly accessible MRI datasets, thereby substantiating a notable enhancement in classification accuracy when compared to single-institution models. The results indicate that the FL approach not only enhances diagnostic accuracy but also facilitates multi-institutional collaborations without compromising patient data privacy. This solution holds promise for widespread clinical adoption, enabling better management and treatment of brain tumors through advanced, privacy-preserving AI techniques.

articleTitle: An Artificial Immune System Algorithm for the Permutation Flow Shop Scheduling Problem with Sequence Dependent Setup Times
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Optimization and Applications (ICOA)
abstract: This paper is concerned with a set of independent jobs in a permutation flow shop that have setup times on a set of machines. The M-IAIS algorithm, which is based on immunoglobulins and has been modified, is designed to reduce the makespan. A unique procedure known as B cell repertoire updating, which comprises size C of jobs that are taken out of the sequence and reinserted into all possible positions of the remaining sequences of jobs, has an impact on the M-IAIS algorithm's performance. To increase the convergence velocity, three iterations of the algorithm are suggested. Thorough testing was done, and the three versions' performances on a set (benchmark) are compared. Problem instances are described in Sistemas de Optimizacion Aplicada (http://soa.iti.es/problem-instances) In the paper, percentage deviation is considered to evaluate the performance of the proposed algorithms. Furthermore, the ensuing outcomes demonstrate its suitability for addressing for the Permutation Flow Shop Scheduling Problem with Sequence Dependent Setup Times.

articleTitle: Predicting Automobile Prices Using Regression Methods and Particle Swarm Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Optimization and Applications (ICOA)
abstract: This study examines automobile price prediction using three distinct regression methods: Ordinary Least Squares (OLS), Ridge Regression, and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). Utilizing data from the UCI Machine Learning Repository, we analyze the performance of these methods in modeling car prices based on engine size and horsepower. We compare OLS, a conventional linear regression technique, with Ridge Regression, which addresses multicollinearity through regularization, and PSO, a metaheuristic optimization method that efficiently handles non-linear relationships and complex data patterns. Performance is assessed using the Mean Squared Error (MSE), providing insights into the effectiveness of each approach. The findings illuminate the trade-offs between simplicity, regularization, and computational efficiency in regression modeling for car pricing, offering valuable insights for both industry practitioners and researchers.

articleTitle: Actuarial Risks Associated to Disease Outbreaks and Insurance Plans Under Media Coverage Strategy
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Optimization and Applications (ICOA)
abstract: In this article, we investigate some of the relevant works that have investigated pandemic risk and the impact of insurance policies. We will present a comprehensive mathematical epidemic model designed to analyze the intricate interplay between insurance plans, media coverage effect, premium reserves and the actual present value of benefit payments in the face of infectious disease outbreaks. Through numerical simulations, we illustrate how media coverage effects impact the adoption and performance of insurance plans, and explore the implications of these effects on the present value of benefit payments and premium reserves.

articleTitle: Optimization of Carbon Emissions in Asphalt Pavement Construction
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Optimization and Applications (ICOA)
abstract: This paper investigates the optimization of carbon emissions in asphalt pavement construction by deep Q-learning. The study developed a model to identify optimal hybrid systems that are environmentally and cost-effective. The optimized system resulted in a 5% reduction in CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions compared to the classical methods, significant improvements in energy consumption, water use and hazardous waste generation in Besides, the inclusion of plastic waste in asphalt mix not only increased the sustainability but also saved costs by 0.8%. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of deep Q-learning to overcome challenging optimization challenges in pavement construction, to promote environmental and economic benefits. Despite the computational demands of the model, the findings highlighted the potential of advanced Deep learning techniques to increase product sustainability and efficiency. The integration of deep Q-learning provides a new approach to construction optimization, significantly reducing carbon emissions and operating costs while promoting sustainable development.

articleTitle: Imaging a Non-Penetrable Target in a Waveguide Using the Topological Derivative
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Optimization and Applications (ICOA)
abstract: Using the topological derivative method, we study the shape reconstruction of a non-penetrable sound-soft obstacle located inside a tubular waveguide. We provide an expression for the topological derivative in terms of the solution of an auxiliary adjoint problem. The behavior of the topological derivative for different scatterer shapes, transducer locations, and numbers of transducers is demonstrated through numerical results in two dimensions.

articleTitle: Leveraging Machine Learning for Anomaly Detection Methods in Cryptocurrency: A Data-Driven Study
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Optimization and Applications (ICOA)
abstract: Cryptocurrencies like Bitcoin and Ethereum have experienced remarkable growth but also high volatility, making anomaly detection crucial for predictive modeling and risk management. This study evaluates three unsupervised machine learning algorithms - Local Outlier Factor, One-Class Support Vector Machine, and Isolation Forest - for detecting anomalies in Bitcoin and Ethereum prices and returns from January 2017 to May 2024. Local Outlier Factor is benchmarked against One-Class Support Vector Machine and Isolation Forest using mean absolute error (MAE), root mean squared error (RMSE), and explained variance score (EVS) as performance metrics. Results demonstrate Local Outlier Factor outperforms One-Class Support Vector Machine and Isolation Forest in detecting return anomalies for both cryptocurrencies. While Local Outlier Factor and Isolation Forest exhibit similar global anomaly detection capability, Local Outlier Factor achieves lower RMSE, indicating superior efficiency in capturing cryptocurrency market dynamics. One-Class Support Vector Machine lagged the other two methods across all metrics. The findings highlight the efficacy of density-based local outlier detection techniques like Local Outlier Factor for cryptocurrency applications. This study provides valuable insights for developing robust anomaly detection systems to enhance risk management and trading strategies in the highly volatile cryptocurrency market.

articleTitle: A Penalization Approach in Breast Cancer Chemotherapy: Preliminary Numerical Simulations
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Optimization and Applications (ICOA)
abstract: In this paper, we discuss preliminary numerical simulation results that stem from an optimal control problem in breast cancer chemotherapy. The objective of this control problem is to minimize the growth of tumor cells while minimizing damage to normal tissue, considering that chemotherapeutic agents affect both tumor cells and healthy cells. The control variable is drug concentration, and the state variable is the tumor density in the breast. We first formulate the optimal control problem by specifying a performance criterion and various constraints and then investigate the necessary optimality conditions. Next, we present an optimization algorithm for solving the control problem. Finally, we present and discuss numerical simulations to demonstrate the importance of the suggested optimal control strategy for tumor cell eradication.

articleTitle: Forecasting Risk Pregnancies in Peru using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Optimization and Applications (ICOA)
abstract: In Peru, between 2017 and 2021, there has been an upward trend in maternal deaths attributed to preeclampsia, reaching an average of 393 cases. Recognizing the importance of early detection of risks associated with preeclampsia, a predictive model was developed using machine learning techniques to forecast pregnancies at risk of preeclampsia. Six models (Support Vector Machine, C5.0 Algorithm, Classification and Regression Trees, k-Nearest Neighbors, Naive Bayes, Logistic Regression) were employed on 44,633 records analyzed from an obstetrics section located in a hospital in Peru, with 11 out of 24 variables selected, including laboratory tests. Logistic Regression demonstrated the best performance, achieving an AUC of 97.6% and an accuracy of 81.8%. This model has the potential to be implemented in hospital settings to detect preeclampsia early, which could significantly contribute to reducing maternal and neonatal mortality rates in the country.

articleTitle: Application of SARSA-Based Reinforcement Learning Approach for Resource Allocation in Vehicular Edge Computing
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Optimization and Applications (ICOA)
abstract: Vehicular Edge Computing (VEC) holds significant promise for enhancing the performance and resource utilization of Internet of Vehicles (loV) applications. However, the dynamic nature of vehicular networks, characterized by high mobility and limited capabilities of VEC servers, poses significant challenges for resource allocation. This paper proposes a Reinforcement Learning (RL) based approach, employing the SARSA algorithm, to learn optimal resource allocation strategies in Multi-access Edge Computing (MEC) environments designed for vehicular networks. Our strategy aims to minimize service delays and balance resource utilization effectively by dynamically deciding whether to offload tasks to edge servers or cloud servers. We evaluate the proposed approach using the EdgeCloudSim simulator, comparing its performance against conventional static and heuristic resource allocation methods. Simulation results, considering various parameters and application characteristics, demonstrate the superior efficiency of our SARSA-based resource allocation solution for VEC compared to traditional methods, in terms of overall service time and resource utilization.

articleTitle: Pedagogical Innovation and Artificial Intelligence in the Service of Entrepreneurial Education: A Proposed Theoretical Anchor
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Optimization and Applications (ICOA)
abstract: Artificial intelligence is at the heart of the evolution that entrepreneurship has undergone. Studying the impact and dynamics between artificial intelligence (AI) and entrepreneurship education is essential to help educators improve efficient pedagogical tools. The adoption and implementation of AI in educational programs offers both opportunities and challenges for teachers and students. One of the challenges for future generations is to identify effective tools and best practices for the integration and adoption of AI in entrepreneurial learning processes. Although the majority of students recognize the value of AI, their interaction with it in the educational context seems less extensive than expected, focusing on a few specific tools. This article proposes a theoretical analysis aimed at supporting pedagogical innovation through AI in the field of entrepreneurial education. In it, we present innovative theoretical models for entrepreneurial universities integrating AI into its educational programs.

articleTitle: Alpine-Peaks Shape of Optimized Configurations Post Random Search in Regional Hydrological LSTMs
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Optimization and Applications (ICOA)
abstract: In hydrological prediction, Long Short-Term Memory networks (LSTMs) hold promise, yet precise hyperparameter tuning remains challenging, especially for regional prediction across multiple catchments. This study addresses the challenge by employing a random search approach to simultaneously tune 10 distinct hyperparameters with two learning rate schedules, for hourly streamflow and water level predictions across 40 catchments in Basque Country, Spain. Exploration of 1000 random configurations revealed an optimization landscape akin to Alpine peaks in the hyperparameters space, with promising settings emerging, each showing high accuracy in several basins, but not everywhere. Post-random search analysis identified top-performing configurations exhibiting consistency in regional metrics but variability in basin-scale performance. Underwent the same training approach, some configurations focused to learn general patterns in as many places as possible; while, some tried to learn anomalies in data such as human fingerprints. Therefore, selecting the optimal regional configuration proved complex due to variations in catchment-scale performance. The Alpine-peaks shape of hyperparameter optimization highlights different learning behaviors by different configurations, emphasizing the importance of ensemble learning for improved predictions across diverse catchments.

articleTitle: An Overview of BTMS for LIB: Opportunities & Challenges
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Optimization and Applications (ICOA)
abstract: Electric vehicles (EVs) are crucial in reducing greenhouse gas emissions, relying on lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) due to their high energy capacity and durability. However, temperature fluctuations can impact LIB performance, affecting capacity, safety, and longevity. This study explores the evolving landscape of thermal management for lithium-ion batteries in response to the growing demand for EVs. It reviews computational and experimental studies from 2013 to 2023, utilizing data from the Web of Science database, and focuses on various cooling systems used in LIBs to address temperature fluctuations. Notably, research efforts significantly increased in 2023, with a balanced focus on cooling technologies. This paper provides a comprehensive review of current methods and advancements in LIB cooling systems, emphasizing the importance of continued research and development to improve battery performance and safety in electric vehicles.

articleTitle: Enhancing Photovoltaic Production Management and Air Conditioning Efficiency in the University Library Smart Building
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Optimization and Applications (ICOA)
abstract: By utilizing various technologies designed to gather, track, and evaluate data, we can maximize energy efficiency and regulate energy use. As a result, a number of solutions were incorporated into the Ibn Tofail University library. We covered the use of photovoltaic generation to power air conditioning in this article. At the smart building level, we were able to gather data on the PV system's energy production and temperature owing to the SCADA monitoring system. Additionally, we were able to collect the frequency of library users by using the SCADA system. These important characteristics were converted into curves that show when the air conditioning systems, which are double fed at their starting mode, should be turned on. We were able to reduce the air conditioning system's demand by 14% because this schedule works with our excess photovoltaic production. Two techniques were applied to deal with these findings.

articleTitle: Efficiency and Optimality in Electrochemical Battery Model Parameter Identification: A Comparative Study of Estimation Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Optimization and Applications (ICOA)
abstract: Parameter identification for electrochemical battery models has always been challenging due to the multitude of parameters involved, most of which cannot be directly measured. This paper evaluates the efficiency and optimality of three widely-used parameter identification methods for electrochemical battery models: Least Squares Method (LS), Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), and Genetic Algorithm (GA). Therefore, a Single Particle Model (SPM) of a battery was developed and discretized. Battery parameter grouping was then performed to reduce the number of parameters required. Using a set of parameters previously identified from a real battery as a benchmark, we generated fitting and validation datasets to assess the methods' runtime and accuracy. The comparative analysis reveals that PSO outperforms the other methods in terms of accuracy and stability, making it highly effective for parameter identification when there is no prior knowledge of the battery's internal parameters. In contrast, LS is better suited for minor adjustments in parameters, particularly for aging batteries, whereas GA lags behind in both computational efficiency and optimality with respect to PSO.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Lightweight Encryption Using SPECK and SIMON for E-Health Using IoT
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Optimization and Applications (ICOA)
abstract: The Internet of Things refers to the interconnected network of physical devices, vehicles, appliances, and other objects embedded with sensors, software, and network connectivity, enabling them to collect and exchange data. The Internet of Things (IoT) has made significant inroads, especially into the healthcare sector, transforming the way medical services are delivered, monitored, and managed. The integration of IoT devices and technologies in healthcare has resulted in improved patient outcomes, enhanced efficiency, and a more proactive approach to healthcare management. the main issues are the protection of sensor data and the availability of appropriate local and global connectivity. In this paper, we are introducing a hybrid Lightweight Encryption using SPECK and SIMON for Healthcare for small sensors and mobile devices. Also, using the Node-RED tool makes the proposal extremely significant.

articleTitle: Integrating TOPSIS-KNN Classifier for Job Market Trends Identification and Employability Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Optimization and Applications (ICOA)
abstract: This paper addresses the growing importance of identifying job market trends and assessing graduate employability amidst technological advancements and market changes. It highlights the function of artificial intelligence, including machine learning and deep learning, in providing adaptive solutions to complex unemployment issues. Key questions explored include methods for identifying trends, criteria for classification, and selection of suitable MCDM methods like AHP and ELECTRE, with TOPSIS identified as optimal. The study also evaluates ten ML models based on accuracy and other metrics to forecast employability and enhance workforce readiness, offering insights for policy-making and educational strategies. The originality of this article lies in the fact that it is the first time an article has merged the two MCDM and ML methods for predicting employability issue, which, in the end, provided satisfying results for the identification of market trends and the prediction of employability.

articleTitle: Lateral Control for Autonomous Vehicles Utilizing an ANN-Based Controller
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Optimization and Applications (ICOA)
abstract: This article investigates the use of artificial intelligence, particularly artificial neural networks (ANNs), to enhance road safety by refining lateral stability and trajectory tracking in autonomous driving systems. ANNs are utilized as control models to optimize the performance of these safety systems. The study employs rigorous methodologies for data collection, neural network training, and thorough testing and validation to evaluate the efficacy of these controllers. The primary goal is to compare the performance of ANN-based controllers with that of established automotive simulation software like Carsim, focusing specifically on metrics related to stability and efficiency. Numerical simulations confirm the validity and effectiveness of the proposed methods, showcasing how AI-driven control systems can significantly improve road safety in autonomous driving scenarios.

articleTitle: Efficient Simulations for Pricing Barrier Options under Stochastic Volatility Model
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Optimization and Applications (ICOA)
abstract: In this work, a numerical method is proposed to evaluate barrier options. We use a classical and recently proposed numerical techniques for derivative pricing with applications to barrier options under stochastic volatility model. Monte-Carlo simulations are used which refer to a set of methods for generating synthetic time series of the volatility and stock price of equities, from which option price can be derived. We present our numerical results; we find that these schemes are intended to have faster convergence.

articleTitle: An Octagonal Patch Antenna for Enhanced 5G Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Optimization and Applications (ICOA)
abstract: In this paper, we present the design of an Octagonal Patch Antenna (OPA) that operates at 28 GHz for 5G applications. This single antenna is printed on top of a Rogers RT5870 substrate with a dielectric constant of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\epsilon_{r}=\mathbf{2.2}$</tex> and a thickness of hs= 1.275 mm. The simulated results offers a wide bandwidth of BW=6.871 GHz with a return loss parameters value of S11= -28.68 dB and a Voltage Standing Wave Ratio (VSWR) value of 1.07. It shows also an important gain of G=6.78 dB, a directivity value of D=8.09 dBi, and efficiency value of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\eta=\mathbf{0.838}$</tex> at its resonant frequency. The presented antenna exhibits good performance for 5G applications. The simulated result were carried out using CST Microwave Studio.

articleTitle: A 2-Parameters Weight Definition in Least-Squares Regression Towards Data Fitting with Uncertainty
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Optimization and Applications (ICOA)
abstract: Linear regression often fits a model to observations without accounting for associated uncertainties, as seen in Ordinary Least Squares (OLS). To address this limitation, a new two-parameter weight system is evaluated within the Weighted Least-Squares (WLS) method, which, unlike OLS, accounts for uncertainty in the observations. The weights are defined by a delay, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\tau$</tex>, and a form factor, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{I}. \tau$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{I}$</tex> modulate the weight based on the observation uncertainty <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sigma_{i}$</tex> and the prediction error <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varepsilon_{i}$</tex>, adapting the weight dynamically depending on their relative values. The weights are tested against known target functions, using the model-to-target distance over a selected interval for various observations errors and number of observations. Estimators using these new weights outperform the naive method (which ignores uncertainty) and are particularly effective when traditional weights, defined as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1/\sigma^{2}$</tex>, are inadequate, such as in homoskedastic scenarios.

articleTitle: Minimizing Non-Quality Costs in Production: A Comprehensive Review of Quality Optimization Strategies
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Optimization and Applications (ICOA)
abstract: This study presents a literature review aimed at informing strategies for reducing non-quality costs in production chains. The main objective is to synthesize existing research to provide information on principles, methodologies, and best practices used in quality optimization and cost reduction. A systematic review approach was adopted to identify relevant work in scientific journals and academic databases. Key terms such as quality, cost, optimization, and reduction were used to ensure the completeness of the review. The selected articles were analyzed to extract relevant information on strategies, techniques, and outcomes associated with the reduction of non-quality costs. This literature review reveals many approaches and methodologies used by organizations to mitigate non-quality costs and improve operational efficiency. Key results include the importance of a holistic approach to quality optimization, including many proactive measures like supply chain management, Lean, and Six Sigma. The article also highlights the importance of organizational culture, leadership commitment, and employee involvement in continuous improvement efforts to reduce costs and improve quality. The review contributes to existing knowledge by synthesizing various research results and presenting a coherent framework to understand the reduction of non-quality costs. By identifying emerging trends, challenges, and opportunities in quality management and cost optimization, this study provides valuable information for academics, practitioners, and decision-makers seeking to improve the performance and competitiveness of organizations in a dynamic business environment.

articleTitle: Optimization and Finite Element Analysis of Scraper Rings in Automotive Gasoline Internal Combustion Engines
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Optimization and Applications (ICOA)
abstract: Automobile engines have evolved significantly over time, improving fuel economy, passenger comfort, and environmental impact. In Internal Combustion Engines, the piston ring is a crucial component, greatly influences overall engine performance. Advances in design, geometry, and materials have enhanced inertia forces and extended replacement intervals. Modern piston rings, often made from cast iron or steel alloys, are optimized to meet stringent functional requirements while reducing their number. This study aims to design a piston ring for a 1000 cc gasoline engine using two materials: Cast Iron (CI) and Steel Alloy. Utilizing 3D modeling software, the piston ring designs are evaluated through finite element analysis (FEA) to assess Von Mises stress and first principal strain. The results are analyzed to identify the optimal piston ring shape, employing numerical methods to predict the lifetime of these mechanical parts in the automotive industry.

articleTitle: A Conceptual Model of Semi-Structured Data for Big Data Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Optimization and Applications (ICOA)
abstract: The vast influx of data has posed significant challenges for major corporations. This deluge has sparked numerous issues within big data, prompting a need for research and industrial solutions. Among the crucial challenges is the requirement for semi-structured data storage and handling to manage large volumes of data with adaptable schemas. Recently, researchers have proposed features and specifications for designing schemas tailored to semi-structured data formats. However, these proposals have not undergone evaluation based on semi-structured properties. Consequently, this study assesses these features within the context of semi-structured properties for big data applications. The findings indicate that semi-structured properties partially or fully support some of these features.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Based Automatic Modulation Classification Using IQ Signals
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Optimization and Applications (ICOA)
abstract: In this study, we explore the application of deep learning techniques for Automatic Modulation Classification (AMC) utilizing In-phase and Quadrature (IQ) signals. Specifically, we leverage the RadioML 2018.01A dataset, which contains various modulation types, to train and evaluate our models. Our approach employs Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to effectively capture both spatial and temporal features inherent in the IQ data. We also experiment with different architectures and hyperparameters to optimize classification performance. The results demonstrate that deep learning methods can achieve high accuracy in identifying modulation schemes, outperforming traditional machine learning techniques. This work highlights the potential of deep learning in enhancing the capabilities of wireless communication systems through improved signal processing and classification.

articleTitle: Pricing Basket Option in Using the Two-Dimensional Black Scholes Equation and the Monte Carlo Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Optimization and Applications (ICOA)
abstract: The purpose of this article is to investigate and use the two-dimensional partial differential Black-Scholes equation using the Monte Carlo method, including Cholesky decomposition to generate correlated Brownian movements, to analyze options on two underlying assets. This study focuses on the performance evaluation and risk management of investment portfolios comprised of these two assets over a given time period. Using a numerical simulation method, this study intends to show how the two-dimensional Black-Scholes model improves the ability to reflect the intricacies of market dynamics with linked assets. The two-dimensional fractional differential equation could be expressed in the form of: \begin{gather*}\frac{\partial\mu}{\partial t}+\frac{1}{2}\sigma_{1}^{2}x^{2}\frac{\partial^{2}\mu}{\partial x^{2}}+\frac{1}{2}\sigma_{2w}^{2}y^{2}\frac{\partial^{2}\mu}{\partial y^{2}}+\rho\sigma_{1}\sigma_{2}xy\frac{\partial^{2}\mu}{\partial x\partial y}\\ +r.\ [x\frac{\partial\mu}{\partial x}+y\frac{\partial\mu}{\partial y}]-r.\mu=0\end{gather*}

articleTitle: Deep Learning Optimizers for Histological Image Classification: A Comparative Study
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Optimization and Applications (ICOA)
abstract: Over the last few years, there has been a great deal of progress in the field of image recognition, using classical or modern methods based on machine learning algorithms. In this context, numerous studies on object detection have been carried out in various fields, with promising results. The aim of this paper is the design of an automatic classification system for tumor tissue cells (breast cancer) in medical images (histological images). The proposed approach relies on the use of convolutional neural networks (CNNs), with numerous experiments using different optimization algorithms such as RMSprop, SGD or Adam to evaluate the performance of our approach. The findings show the effectiveness of the RMSprop optimizer, with a fast convergence rate and high accuracy.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Integration in Supplier Relationship Management for Enhanced Stock Management
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Optimization and Applications (ICOA)
abstract: In today's modern age, technology has evolved in many aspects of day-to-day life, from the simplest task to the more complicated one. Therefore, companies are relying on modern development which is based on software engineering and digitalization to sustain their business growth and competitive advantages.

articleTitle: MOOC Drop-Out Prediction Based on Learners Sentiment Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Optimization and Applications (ICOA)
abstract: Despite the progress and appeal of MOOCs as an accessible and inexpensive online learning mode, retention rates remain minimal. There are several reasons for this, including the lack of interaction, the approaches used in course design and presentation, as well as factors related to students' cognitive aspects, their representations, and the obstacles encountered along the way. It is therefore essential to understand students' opinions in the context of MOOCs, using discussion forums as a means of interaction where learners can share their experiences. This paper presents a method for predicting the risk of dropping out of a MOOC by analyzing learners' sentiments in their forum comments. The approach is based on a detailed process of textual data preparation, including cleaning, transliteration, and tokenization. Then, we extract relevant features that feed into a logistic regression model using advanced natural language processing techniques. This predictive model enables us to estimate the risk of dropping out based on student satisfaction, providing a valuable tool for identifying and intervening with at-risk learners.

articleTitle: Predictive Modeling for Economic Implications of COVID-19: Unraveling Patterns and Vulnerabilities Through Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Optimization and Applications (ICOA)
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic brought sweeping changes to everyone's economic activities, leaving small-scale and large businesses alike shaken at their bottom line, and governments, including ours, were forced to avert a further global economic collapse. This research discusses an approach based on predictive modeling for the purpose of predicting the economic consequences of COVID-19 for individuals using the machine learning and data driven methods. The study aims to create a predictive model based on RapidMiner software, which will enable the authorities to anticipate a COVID-19's economic crisis and reveal important predictors of the impact. By conducting data analyses and recommendations from the projected models, the result shows a significant impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on different demographics and provides guidelines to policymakers and credible sources. This paper makes a useful contribution for informed decision making and the development of special strategies to counteract crisis' negative impacts and build economic resilience.

articleTitle: Predictive Analytics for Enhanced Passenger Satisfaction in the Airline Industry: Leveraging Machine Learning to Drive Strategic Decision-Making
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Optimization and Applications (ICOA)
abstract: In the highly competitive airline industry, enhancing passenger satisfaction is crucial for maintaining customer loyalty and market competitiveness. This study utilizes advanced machine learning techniques to analyze comprehensive dataset comprising approximately 130,000 entries related to airline passenger experiences. The dataset includes both qualitative and quantitative attributes from in-flight services to logistical details of air travel. Two predominant machine learning models, Naive Bayes and k-Nearest Neighbors (k-NN) were employed to predict passenger satisfaction levels and identify key factors impacting their experience. The Naive Bayes model demonstrated superior predictive performance compared to k-NN, with significant accuracy, precision, recall, and AUC metrics. This research not only offers valuable insights into the key factors influencing passenger satisfaction but also provides data-driven recommendations for service improvement. It lays the groundwork for airlines to utilize predictive analytics in strategic decision-making, thereby enhancing passenger satisfaction and operational efficiency.

articleTitle: Integration of Machine Learning Algorithms and Nash Game Theory in A Similar Image Retrieval System
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Optimization and Applications (ICOA)
abstract: In the realm of image processing, the ability to describe an image accurately and comprehensively is paramount. Images, whether captured by cameras, generated by computers, or obtained through various means, contain a wealth of information waiting to be analyzed and understood. Among the key elements defining an image, two stand out prominently: color and form. Each of these components plays a crucial role in shaping our perception and interpretation of visual data. Our team has crafted a CBIR system enhanced by a duo of machine learning algorithms and various clustering techniques alongside low-level image feature extraction methods. These components converge to formulate a Nash game, thereby presenting us with a multi-criteria optimization challenge. In tackling this challenge, we've devised a In this two-player static Nash game, each player employs a unique strategy, specifically color moments and shape moments, corresponding to their objective functions. The Nash equilibrium is represented by the membership classes assigned to the query image. Looking ahead, we intend to replace the Zernike moments with a neural network approach and thoroughly compare the two methods concerning time and efficiency

articleTitle: A Foundational Framework for an UAV GPS Jamming Simulator
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Optimization and Applications (ICOA)
abstract: This paper presents a theoretical framework for a GPS signals jamming simulator designed to evaluate the effects of jamming on a GPS receiver onboard a UAV in an aerodynamic environment. This methodological study focuses on modeling the jammer, the GPS receiver, the propagation environment, and the electronic attack scenario. While commercially available GNSS jamming simulators exist, they can be expensive due to their complexity. This proposed simulator offers an alternative approach to assess the reliability of GPS observables like pseudo ranges, carrier phases, and Doppler measurements under jamming attacks. Furthermore, the framework allows for the exploration and development of anti-jamming techniques capable of detection, mitigation, and localization of interference sources.

articleTitle: Digital Banking Issues Experienced by Older People
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Optimization and Applications (ICOA)
abstract: Nowadays, digital banking is a crucial component of contemporary financial systems, providing customers all over the world with efficiency and comfort. However, using digital banking platforms presents special difficulties for older persons, which can obstruct their ability to be financially independent and included. The purpose of this research abstract is to investigate and clarify the challenges older people have when embracing and using digital financial services. Based on extant literature and practical investigations, this study highlights multiple significant obstacles encountered by senior citizens when it comes to digital banking. These difficulties include technological impediments that make it difficult for older consumers to access and efficiently use online banking services, such as low digital literacy and unfamiliarity with digital platforms. In addition, intricate user interfaces and security issues compound these difficulties, causing older people to become frustrated and anxious. Moreover, insufficient accessibility features and a lack of tailored support on digital banking platforms further marginalize senior citizens and hinder their capacity to interact with financial services on their own. Furthermore, in the context of digital banking, older persons' sentiments of alienation and loneliness are made worse by the absence of strong support networks and mentorship. This research attempts to provide light on the various difficulties older individuals encounter when using digital banking through an extensive assessment and analysis of the body of previous knowledge. Understanding these issues can help policymakers, financial institutions, and tech developers create more focused interventions and inclusive digital banking solutions that meet the varied needs of senior citizens. This will promote senior citizens' financial inclusion and empowerment in the digital age.

articleTitle: Prediction Analysis for Demand Forcasting in Automotive Industry
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Optimization and Applications (ICOA)
abstract: Effectively managing risks in the supply chain is a critical aspect of modern business operations, and predictive analysis emerges as a key tool in business. This topic explores the application of predictive analysis to anticipate and mitigate risks within the supply chain. The article delves into the use of machine learning models to early detect potential issues, providing a proactive approach to risk management. Through an examination of case studies, the paper highlights the impact of predictive analysis on reducing vulnerabilities and enhancing the resilience of the supply chain. The research aims to shed light on the practical implementation of predictive analysis for risk management, offering insights to both industry practitioners and researchers.

articleTitle: Predictive Control for Sustainable Greenhouses
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Optimization and Applications (ICOA)
abstract: The agricultural sector is a cornerstone of many countries' economies, and recently its methods have evolved to enhance productivity while balancing economic growth with environmental protection. This study explores the adoption of intelligent techniques in a smart greenhouse integrated micro-grid considered as an avenue for increasing the productivity in a sustainable way. The paper includes the regulation of the greenhouse microclimate based on a predictive controller, as well as its integration into a micro-grid.

articleTitle: Review of Dynamic Spectrum Sharing: Techniques and Challenges
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Optimization and Applications (ICOA)
abstract: It appears that the frequency bands used by the current mobile network are becoming increasingly scarce, making it impossible for it to meet the overwhelming demand brought on by the introduction of 5G and the rapidly growing popularity of IOT devices. It is evident that due to spectrum shortage, the traditional method of statically allocating spectrum to particular services or users became systematically inefficient and unsustainable. As a result, it is time for a wireless communication system to emerge that allows multiple users or wireless systems to share radio frequency spectrum in real-time and efficiently. It's DSS ( dynamic spectrum sharing), a revolutionary approach that allows different wireless technologies to dynamically share the same spectrum resources based on demand and usage patterns. This dynamic allocation is typically facilitated by advanced spectrum management techniques and intelligent algorithms that we are going to provide in this article in addition to the challenges that this technology has to face.

articleTitle: Optimizing Spare Parts Inventory Management Using Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Optimization and Applications (ICOA)
abstract: Having spare components on hand is essential to keeping systems operating at their best. Many scholars have looked into problems with inventory management for spare parts over the last decades. Proving that (s,S) policies are optimal for specific dynamic inventory models with random periodic requests has been a major contribution to inventory theory. The widely used maintenance models make the assumption that there is an endless supply of replacement parts. Nonetheless, in certain real-life scenarios, the availability of spare components plays a significant role in choosing the best course of action for the entire system. The main goal from this research is to minimize management expenses by identifying the most efficient method for figuring out how much spare parts to order at each period. These expenses cover a range of charges related to inventory management. In order to reach all that, the study suggests a mathematical framework which relies on a Markov decision model, and then solve the optimality equation and derive optimal (s, S) policies through the application of the recurrence approach. As for the part of numeric, the paper is also presenting a new method that introduces genetic algorithms for the maximization of the service levels and the minimization of the expenses at the same time. After all, this work aims to establish strong inventory management plans for a variable periodic demand inventory model, which will guarantee effective resource allocation and operational excellence.

articleTitle: A Deep Learning-Based Model for Malware Detection Using Transformer Architecture
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Optimization and Applications (ICOA)
abstract: This research presents a new Transformer-based deep learning malware detection system for Portable Executables on Windows. The system analyzed a dataset of 11,000 executables, containing 8,700 malware and 2,300 benign files from VirusTotal, and demonstrated the ability of Transformers to learn highly complex patterns from assembly code. The system's multilevel architecture includes disassembly, tokenization, and feature extraction, allowing it to discriminate between malicious and benign files with great accuracy. The Transformer model, through its self-attention mechanisms, achieves better learning dynamics and higher accuracy compared to traditional models. Preliminary results show high precision in detecting malware, indicating the potential for Transformers to significantly enhance cybersecurity and address increasing threats.

articleTitle: Road Marking Detection and Instance Segmentation Using YOLOv8 Models
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Optimization and Applications (ICOA)
abstract: This paper investigates the concepts of road marking detection and instance segmentation in the context of autonomous driving. It discusses the significance of these tasks and their applications in traffic analysis and road safety. The paper highlights the role of instance segmentation in enhancing object detection, tracking, semantic mapping, and scene understanding in autonomous driving systems. It emphasizes the benefits of instance segmentation in improving precision, handling occlusions, and enhancing association and track maintenance. The paper also evaluates the YOLOv8 model's performance in road marking detection and instance segmentation. The evaluation dataset comprises 2885 images with 11 classes of road markings captured in diverse weather conditions. Various sizes of YOLOv8 models are thoroughly assessed to measure their effectiveness in addressing these tasks.

articleTitle: Generic Formulation of the Requirements Selection Problem
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Optimization and Applications (ICOA)
abstract: Selecting the appropriate requirements to develop in the next release of a software product is a complex multi-criteria decision process that has been solved by several optimisation approaches. However, there is neither a unified nor a general formulation that could manage the currently agreed properties and relationships between requirements. This paper presents a generic formulation for this problem, which can be tailored to each specific problem, and also allows for its extension in the future. The implementation of six case studies to demonstrate the successful adaptation of the generic formulation is also described.

articleTitle: Backtracking Search Algorithm with Lemur Optimizer for Numerical and Global Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Optimization and Applications (ICOA)
abstract: The Backtracking Search Algorithm (BSA) stands out as a contemporary stochastic technique that has showcased its prowess in tackling intricate engineering challenges. Thus, a novel hybrid evolutionary algorithm designed to fully leverage the advantages of the BSA and the Lemurs Optimizer (LO). The core objective of this hybrid algorithm is to enhance and discover the global search ability of BSA and provide a robust optimization tool for finding global optima or high-quality solutions for a variety of complex benchmark functions commonly used in the field of optimization. LOBSA's effectiveness has been put to the test with 23 diverse benchmark functions, and its performance has been evaluated through a comparison with highly regarded state-of-the-art competitors. Besides, statistical results indicate that LOBSA presents promising and competitive outcomes, not only for its initial variant but also when compared to the other algorithms.

articleTitle: Genghis Khan Shark Optimizer Based Approach for Multi-Objective Engineering Problems
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Optimization and Applications (ICOA)
abstract: This study introduces a new multi-objective approach called the Non-Dominated Genghis Khan Shark Opti-mizer (NSGKSO) for tackling mechanical engineering challenges. The GKSO's inspiration is derived from the natural behaviors of GKS, structuring its process of optimization by mimicking four specific behaviors of GKSs: exploration (hunting), exploitation (movement), transitioning from exploration to exploitation (foraging), and a self-defense mechanism. Following the elitist non-dominated sorting mechanism in the NSGKSO algorithm, a non-dominated ranking approach is combined with a crowding distance calculation. This integration aims to archive the Pareto front and enhance the coverage of optimal solutions. For evaluating the performance of NSGKSO, a series of benchmark tests are conducted, encompassing standard constrained and unconstrained optimization functions, along with four mechanical engineering design problems. The study includes a comparative analysis between the proposed NSGKSO technique and other established evolutionary optimization methods. Statistical findings showcase the robustness of the NSGKSO approach, assessed through metrics such as inverted generational distance (IGD), generalized distance (GD), and spacing (SP). Moreover, qualitative experimental outcomes affirm that NSGKSO offers highly precise approximations of the real Pareto front.

articleTitle: Optimizing the Validation Process of Resistance Spot Welds in the Automotive Industry Using TOPSIS and K-Fold Cross-Validation
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Optimization and Applications (ICOA)
abstract: In a complex and constantly evolving environment, decision-making has become a major challenge for organizations, governments, and individuals. Faced with this complexity, Multi-Criteria Decision Making (MCDM) methods have proven to be valuable tools. Among them, the TOPSIS (Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution) technique stands out for its ability to provide informed and justified decisions. This issue is particularly relevant in the automotive industry, where resistance spot welding plays a critical role in the assembly of car bodies. However, the choice of optimal welding parameters requires taking into account many conflicting criteria. In this conference paper, we will present the results of training an artificial neural network, with the objective of classifying and validating weld spots according to their dimensions, indentations, and sheet thicknesses. This innovative approach aims to optimize the resistance spot welding process in the automotive industry, leveraging the advancements in artificial intelligence.

articleTitle: A Reconductoring Approach for Efficient Long-Term Planning of the Ecuadorian Power Grid
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Optimization and Applications (ICOA)
abstract: Since 2023, Ecuador has faced significant challenges in the energy sector due to regional droughts impacting hydroelectric capacity and increasing reliance on energy imports. In this context, planning the expansion of the infrastructure that generates and transmits electricity to end consumers should focus on strategies that optimize the use of available resources. This paper presents a Mixed Integer Linear Programming (MILP) approach for multistage combined electricity generation and transmission planning (GTEP). The model employs a reconductoring strategy for existing 230 kV transmission lines, integrating higher-capacity conductors. The practicality and effectiveness of the model are validated through a case study of Ecuador's power system, which features a 21-bus system. The results confirm that the model provides cost-efficient solutions, with a projected investment of $4417.40 MUSD to diversify energy sources and reduce reliance on imports, a crucial step towards achieving Ecuador's energy independence by 2030.

articleTitle: A Robust Cold-Start Approach Using Phylogram
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Optimization and Applications (ICOA)
abstract: In Active Learning (AL) applications, it is crucial to develop a model that efficiently represents data using a limited number of labeled samples. In this context, an oracle is often employed to label samples that are deemed representative and informative. However, one of the primary limitations of AL lies in the need for an initial set of labeled samples, which may not be representative of the entire data space. To address this issue, cold-start strategies are implemented with the goal of selecting an appropriate initial set of samples for labeling, ensuring that the initial model is robust and effective. We propose a novel approach – PhyIL – that harness the advantages of phylogram analysis and community detection techniques to smartly perform the cold-start selection in AL. The method facilitates the choice of samples that best represent the diversity and complexity of the data, which is fundamental for the subsequent success of the active learning process. We evaluated the proposed approach using nine real-world databases and nine traditional ML models. The findings indicate that PhyIL offers an effective and viable solution for the initial sample selection, when compared to the random selection.

articleTitle: The Role of Predictive Maintenance Optimization Techniques in Enhancing Industrial Productivity
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Optimization and Applications (ICOA)
abstract: The convergence between advanced technology and industrial production holds significant potential to enhance operational efficiency, reduce maintenance costs, and minimize unexpected disruptions. Artificial intelligence, in particular, plays a crucial role in predicting machine failures, thereby contributing to the optimization of operational performance and maximizing overall company output. However, current challenges in maintenance and production are numerous. High maintenance costs are often a major concern for companies, as they can significantly eat into profit margins. Unexpected downtime, caused by sudden machine failures, leads to substantial production losses, affecting not only revenue but also customer satisfaction and the company's reputation. Furthermore, the increasing complexity of industrial systems makes the management of maintenance and production even more difficult, necessitating more advanced and integrated solutions. This article explores the various applications of artificial intelligence in the manufacturing industry, highlighting its impact on business performance. It also examines the steps necessary for implementing predictive maintenance, from data collection and processing to the establishment of predictive models. The ultimate goal is to improve equipment availability, optimize operational performance, and maximize overall company output.

articleTitle: Inventory Management in Blood Supply Chain: Future Research Challenges and Opportunities
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Optimization and Applications (ICOA)
abstract: Nowadays, the awareness of the value of healthcare systems management has increased, due to facing an important number of pandemics, disasters either with natural causes or anthropogenic ones. In this paper, the blood supply chain (BSC), a crucial part of the healthcare system, will be analyzed, since lack of blood or its insufficient causes an enormous direct impact on patients' lives and medicine production. Therefore, every hospital must ensure proper logistic management to avoid shortage or wastage. Indeed, this paper discusses BSC inventory which is an important strategic element in this logistic chain. The real challenge in BSC management is the uncertainty of the demand and the raw material availability, considering the only suppliers of blood products are the donors, and its demand is hard to estimate since it is related to the medical case's needs. Therefore, the objective of the proposed paper is to analyze the logistics and supply chain of blood product inventory, with the aim of enhancing awareness and understanding of the challenges, costs, disaster impacts, and current optimization methods associated with blood inventory management. Additionally, the paper examines existing studies to identify unexplored opportunities and to suggest constructive future research directions for the optimization of inventory management logistics.

Author Keywords: logistics engineering in blood supply chain

articleTitle: Automated Software Testing Using Machine Learning: A Systematic Mapping Study
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Optimization and Applications (ICOA)
abstract: In today's digital world, software quality assurance is a crucial part of the Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC), and automated testing is essential to this effort. This study investigates how machine learning (ML) can augment automated testing by analyzing research from 2006 onward to determine its possible uses, prevalent techniques, and related advantages and disadvantages. Our findings reveal a growing interest in leveraging ML for testing, particularly in tasks like test case generation and user interface validation. Common ML techniques such as symbolic AI, evolutionary algorithms, and deep learning are emerging as the primary methods. ML holds promise for accelerating testing processes, enhancing accuracy, and improving adaptability. However, challenges such as sourcing high-quality training data, understanding complex ML models, and integrating ML with existing tools persist. This study illuminates the transformative potential of ML in testing and provides valuable insights for guiding future research in this dynamic field.

articleTitle: A Systematic Review of Blockchain Applications in Pharmaceutical Supply Chain Traceability and Security
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Optimization and Applications (ICOA)
abstract: The pharmaceutical supply chain (PSC) encounters significant challenges, including inefficiencies, lack of transparency, and security vulnerabilities, which facilitate the proliferation of counterfeit drugs and pose serious health risks to patients. Traditional systems, such as centralized databases, barcodes, QR codes, RFID technology, and ERP systems, have been employed for control and traceability but demonstrate substantial limitations. This systematic review examines the transformative potential of blockchain technology to address these critical issues and enhance PSC traceability, security, and efficiency. Blockchain technology, with its core properties of decentralization, immutability, and transparency, offers robust solutions for improving drug authenticity and securing sensitive data. This review highlights the benefits of blockchain implementations through various case studies and pilot projects. It emphasizes the need for future research in scalable, cost-effective methods that balance transparency and data privacy. By overcoming these challenges, blockchain can revolutionize the PSC, ensuring compliance with regulatory standards, countering the risks of counterfeit drugs, and constructing a more resilient and trustworthy supply chain. The integration of blockchain technology in the PSC holds immense potential to enhance security, efficiency, and transparency, thereby safeguarding public health and restoring stakeholder confidence in pharmaceutical products. This systematic review aims to bridge the gap by providing comprehensive insights into the transformative capabilities of blockchain technology in the pharmaceutical sector.

articleTitle: System for Table Run Strategy in Peruvian Billiards with Real-Time Oject Detection using YOLOv8n
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Optimization and Applications (ICOA)
abstract: The main challenge for billiard players, regardless of their skill level, is to develop a strategy that allows them to consecutively pocket balls in a single turn, commonly known as “closing the table.” This strategy requires high precision and consistency, especially for less experienced players. This study integrates a YOLOv8n model, a shot suggestion algorithm, and a shot prediction algorithm to build a system that aids players in developing this “table closing” strategy through visual guides indicating the shots to take and where to position the cue ball for the next shot. The proposed system follows these phases: (1) Selection of the video camera, (2) Selection of the object detection technique, (3) Development of the shot suggestion algorithm, (4) Development of the shot prediction algorithm, and (5) System construction. Phases (1) and (2) address the implementation of the YOLOv8n model, while phases (3) and (4) involve the development of algorithms for the “table closing” strategy. To validate the system's effectiveness, an experiment with 24 players of different skill levels was conducted, showing that the system reduced the average number of shots needed to close a table to 22, compared to the 47-shot average of professional players. Beginners accepted 100% of the system's recommendations, while intermediate and professional players showed acceptance rates of 95.1% and 95.6%, respectively. A survey indicated high overall satisfaction, with a median response of 4.5 on a 5-point scale. The system also demonstrates significant competitive advantages over existing solutions by maintaining high detection and prediction accuracy while effectively functioning in real-world scenarios, leveraging the latest advances in computer vision to surpass older techniques in both effectiveness and efficiency.

articleTitle: Mitigating Online Microgrid Controller Deployment Issues with Learning Techniques: An Approximate MPC Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Optimization and Applications (ICOA)
abstract: Due to the increasing complexity of energy systems, standard rule-based controllers may become inadequate for Energy Management System (EMS) supervision. Advanced optimal techniques as Model Predictive Control (MPC) can be too intensive in computational resources, especially for small agents with low-performance environment. Therefore, control issues about reducing implementation complexity gains interest in literature. In particular, surrogate models integrating learning techniques come within this scope by mitigating online implementation issues with offline data-driven approximations. However, there is a lack of works dealing with the analysis of performance robustness of such approximate controllers, when any uncertainties occur in online control. In this paper, we propose a freestanding approximate explicit MPC method, mobilizing learning techniques that approximate an analytical control law derived from a formal multiparametric programming. We propose to characterize the performance of the so-called reduced controller on simulation of a PV-storage microgrid, with historical data and forecast mismatch. We found numerically that the reduced controller has very similar performances compared to the baseline MPC when the forecast error is approximatively limited to 20%, and globally presents a relative change of economical loss less than 4% in average on simulation tests.

articleTitle: Numerical Solution of Intuitionistic Fuzzy Differential Equations by Nyström Method
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Optimization and Applications (ICOA)
abstract: In this study, different computational techniques for solving fuzzy first-order initial value issues are discussed. We propose a numerical approach based on the Nyström method. Sufficient conditions for the suggested algorithms' stability and convergence are provided, and their application is illustrated through examples.

articleTitle: Comparison of Silver and Gold Based Plasmonic Square Ring Resonator with MIM Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Optimization and Applications (ICOA)
abstract: In this comparative analysis of silver and gold based plasmonic square ring resonator with MIM waveguide filled with analyte from 1 to 1.3. The various sensing parameters such as sensitivity, FOM and Q factor are compared for both gold and silver based substrate. The sensor shows the highest sensitivity 440 nm/RIU with silver and 396 nm/ RIU with gold. Besides this, the highest value of FOM is 31.426 with gold and 30 with silver. The maximum Q-factor is 28.65 with silver as well as 26.428 with gold. The analysis shows silver is dominating over gold for refractive index based sensor including chemical and biological sensing applications because of its reduced cost, enhance sensitivity, anti-bacterial and anti-fungal properties.

articleTitle: Advanced Machine Learning Techniques for Predicting Precious Metal Prices in Financial Trading
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Optimization and Applications (ICOA)
abstract: In an environment as intricate as the financial markets, where fortunes can shift in an instant, the prices of gold, silver, and oil emerge as puzzles, their fluctuations shrouded in mystery. These precious commodities, valued for their intrinsic worth and myriad applications, have long captivated both traders and investors. Today, technological advancements in machine learning play an increasingly crucial role in analyzing these fluctuations, thereby influencing market trends and contributing to shaping global economies. In this context, our aim is to design an intelligent system capable of accurately predicting the prices of gold, silver, and oil in the financial markets. The convergence of cutting-edge technology and financial strategies is essential to understanding and anticipating the movements of precious metal prices. Sophisticated algorithms such as Random Forest Regression (RFR), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, and Support Vector Regression (SVR) allow us to explore new horizons in forecasting market trends. This study delves into this technological and financial convergence, paving the way for redefining the boundaries of precious metal price prediction through artificial intelligence, offering more precise and informed investment strategies, and thereby contributing to the evolution of practices in the financial sector.

articleTitle: Enhancing Educational Feedback Systems using Deep Queue-Dependent Networking: An Automatic StudentAssessment with AI
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Optimization and Applications (ICOA)
abstract: In the field of educational technology, the enhancement of student learning through personalized feedback mechanisms is of utmost importance. This paper investigates the potential of Deep Queue-Dependent Networking (DQN) to transform educational feedback systems, automating student assessment processes. By utilizing artificial intelligence (AI) techniques, particularly reinforcement learning, the proposed approach aims to enhance the efficacy and effectiveness of feedback delivery in educational environments. With DQN in place, the system will independently evaluate student performance, identify areas for improvement, and tailor feedback responses based on individual learning needs. The seamless integration of AI-driven assessment tools will enable educators to streamline the feedback process, offer timely interventions, and foster more engaging and adaptive student learning experiences. This research contributes to the ongoing conversation about applying advanced technologies in education, instilling hope about the potential of DQN-based systems to improve learning outcomes and student success.

articleTitle: Exploring the Use of Machine Learning and the Internet of Things in Intelligent Agriculture: Short Survey
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Optimization and Applications (ICOA)
abstract: Agriculture is evolving towards more sustainable practices thanks to the integration of the machine learning and Internet of Things, which addresses many of the issues related to agricultural production and leads to increased yields with reduced input and labor costs. Smart farming has developed solutions to many conventional agricultural problems to automatically manage and monitor farmland. These technologies reduce the risk of field management in the event of bad weather, and also provide benefits to farmers in the event of labor shortages. The Internet of Things ensures the connection of physical objects that are equipped with sensors to the internet, enabling them to collect and exchange data and communicate with each other and with computer systems to gather information, perform analysis and take actions in real time that require rapid data analysis, and this task can be accomplished through machine learning algorithms with greater efficiency and high-quality decision-making. In addition, we carry out an in-depth state-of-the-art survey to identify very recent work that has implemented the Internet of Things and machine learning in smart agriculture, analyzing the development of practical solutions and discussing recent research trends and future prospects.

articleTitle: Enhanced Banking Security: Isolation Forest with Attention Mechanism for Sophisticated Fraud Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Optimization and Applications (ICOA)
abstract: As digital banking gains appeal, the possibility of fraudulent activity grows, necessitating ongoing developments in fraud detection systems to prevent fund losses. The present study introduces a novel strategy for detecting fraud in the banking industry that uses isolation forests and attention mechanisms. The Isolation Forest (Iforest) technique detects abnormalities in huge datasets, and the Attention Mechanism improves the model's attention to essential characteristics for greater accuracy. Unlike traditional approaches, our model recognizes the underlying sequential character of banking transaction data, allowing for the exact detection of suspicious actions. Experimental assessments confirm the efficacy and efficiency of our technique, indicating a big step forward in strengthening security measures in the banking business.

articleTitle: Towards a CPS Solution for Modeling and Control of Phosphoric Acid Quality
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Optimization and Applications (ICOA)
abstract: Industries are leveraging advanced technologies like digital twins, cyber-physical systems (CPS), and Distribution Control Systems (DCS) to enhance efficiency and maintain competitiveness. Digital twins offer real-time representations of assets, enabling predictive maintenance and decision-making, while CPS integrate hardware and software for process automation and quality improvement. DCS provide centralized control and real-time monitoring, further optimizing operations.
