Ac-curate prediction of P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf>concentration is vital for product quality and process efficiency, yet challenging due to complex influencing factors. Machine learning techniques will be evaluated to identify the best performing model. The results will contribute to better production control and decision-making, with implications for improving industrial standards and sustainability.

articleTitle: Utilizing AI to Tackle Child Overnutrition in Morocco
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Optimization and Applications (ICOA)
abstract: This study investigates the predictive power of various machine learning classifiers in identifying overnutrition among children under five years old in Morocco. Using data from the 2018 national population and family health survey, the research employs ten machine learning algorithms: Logistic Regression, Support Vector Machines (SVM), Gradient Boosting, Random Forest, XGBoost, k-Nearest Neighbors, Decision Trees, Naive Bayes, Artificial Neural Networks, and Deep Learning models. The performance of these models was assessed using accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, kappa statistic, and area under the curve (AUC). The results reveal that Logistic Regression and SVM were the most effective models, achieving nearly ninety percent accuracy for predicting overweight and approximately ninety-seven percent accuracy for predicting obesity. These models also demonstrated high sensitivity and specificity. Gradient Boosting and Random Forest also showed strong performance, while Naive Bayes, despite its lower accuracy, excelled in AUC, indicating its proficiency in overall class distinction. The findings highlight the significant roles of birth weight, socioeconomic status, and parental education in influencing childhood overnutrition. By focusing on the Moroccan context, this study addresses a gap in the existing literature and provides actionable insights for developing targeted public health interventions. The study underscores the effectiveness of Logistic Regression and SVM in handling complex datasets and the importance of early life factors, socioeconomic status, and parental education. The research suggests the need for incorporating more recent and longitudinal data, exploring a broader range of variables, and employing advanced machine learning techniques in future studies to enhance predictive accuracy into the determinants of childhood overnutrition.

articleTitle: Optimizing Cryptocurrency Portfolio Management: Deep Learning with Diverse Data Sources and Multiple Parameters
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Optimization and Applications (ICOA)
abstract: Portfolio optimization is a key area in financial engineering, aiming to maximize investor returns. In this study, we propose an innovative portfolio management system based on Deep Reinforcement learning. Unlike traditional approaches, our system incorporates five parameters, including trading volume, for a more comprehensive market analysis. Furthermore, we leverage multiple data sources simultaneously, providing a more robust perspective. Our approach also stands out by utilizing specially designed deep convolution to separately address each parameter. Additionally, we introduce a five-dimensional attention gating network to better identify critical moments and high-potential assets. Simulation results demonstrate that our approach significantly outperforms traditional methods, offering investors more substantial returns and reduced short-term risk.

articleTitle: IIOT and Deep Learning for Decision-Making: Heading Towards Intelligent Maintenance
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Optimization and Applications (ICOA)
abstract: Traditional maintenance (TM) practices in industrial companies reveal several drawbacks. It is predominantly conducted on fixed schedules rather than based on actual equipment conditions, resulting in issues such as downtime and additional maintenance costs. These issues stem from a lack of real-time data and precise diagnostics, making early detection of failures challenging. This underscores the increasing importance of Industry 4.0 (I4), particularly Predictive maintenance (PM) or what is known as Maintenance 4.0. The latter leverages real-time operational data and sophisticated techniques like data analytics, Machine learning (ML), and peep learning (DL) to anticipate failures in advance. This approach helps reduce maintenance costs and unplanned downtime.

articleTitle: The Role of Artificial Intelligence in the Semantic Web
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Optimization and Applications (ICOA)
abstract: The concept of the Semantic Web is to enhance the web's intelligence and connectivity by enabling machines to process information in a way that resembles understanding. This article delves into how Artificial Intelligence (AI) plays a role in advancing the capabilities of the Semantic Web. By incorporating AI tools like Natural Language Processing (NLP) machine learning and automated reasoning the Semantic Web can exploit the increasing amount of web data available. This integration leads to data accuracy, search functionalities and personalized user experiences. Nonetheless merging AI with the Semantic Web poses challenges such as algorithms, interoperability issues and ethical considerations. Through an examination of current research and practical examples this article sheds light on both the advantages and drawbacks of this fusion while suggesting future research paths to tackle existing obstacles and fully leverage AIs potential within the Semantic Web domain. The paper emphasizes how AI is reshaping interactions, on the Semantic Web towards more effective online engagement.

articleTitle: The Adoption of Sustainability for Sovereign Risk Assessment in UAE: Investigation of Challenges Using MCDM Method
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Optimization and Applications (ICOA)
abstract: This study focuses on understanding the interrelationship between the major challenges for sustainable sovereign credit assessment in UAE. The growth of sustainable investments with sovereign entities has redefined the credit assessment methods for achieving Sustainable Development Goals. It has become vital for The United Arab Emirates (UAE) to cope with the complicated dynamics of sovereign debt while simultaneously addressing environmental and social concerns. The study aims to prioritize and understand the relationship between these challenges by using a multi-criteria decision-making approach of fuzzy DEMATEL (Decision Making Trial and Evaluation Laboratory) method. This study identifies the sovereign credit challenges encountered in UAE related to environmental, social and governance (ESG) principles and sustainability. Fuzzy set theory is used with DEMATEL to map the uncertainty and subjectivity in the decision-making process in the face of sustainability inclusion in UAE. The results show that Political Instability and lack of Standardization are the most important challenges for sovereign credit assessment in UAE. There is a need for the regulatory authority to redefine its strategies to build a more stabilized political environment and simultaneously develop and implement uniform norms and practices across the region that can streamline cross-border investments and trade, enhancing economic integration.

articleTitle: A new Hybrid Metaheuristic Algorithm based Human Approach for Mechanical Engineering Problems
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Optimization and Applications (ICOA)
abstract: This research work develops a novel hybrid optimization algorithm called Technical and Vocational Education and Training based Particle Swarm Optimization (TVETPSO), which incorporates Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) inspired human learning approach in combination with Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) leveraging several mechanisms features as well as involving further learning phases in the proposed TVETPSO, which permit a knowledge transferring and historical generations stored. This human inspired approach allow TVETPSO algorithm to refine its exploration strategies, improve exploitation of the solutions and avoid premature convergence. Where is validated by a diverse set of Benchmark functions and measured in Design Problems such as Welded beam, Gear Train and Tension/Compression Spring. This experiments show an effective behavior against the comparative analysis of the proposed TVETPSO for solving engineering design problems. Ultimately this study offers a robust means for refining an effective resolution of real world optimization problems.

Author Keywords: Technical and vocational education and training (TVET)

articleTitle: Deep Learning for Future: Advancements and Prospects in Signal Denoising for Cognitive Radio
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Optimization and Applications (ICOA)
abstract: Within communication systems, the challenge of noise and interference presents a formidable barrier to reliable data transmission. While classical denoising methods have provided valuable insights, their limitations impede their effectiveness. However, the emergence of deep learning offers a promising solution, especially within the domain of cognitive radio. Deep learning techniques exhibit remarkable efficacy in addressing noise and interference across various signal types. Recent research emphasizes the transformative potential of deep learning in advancing signal denoising methodologies, highlighting its pivotal role in bolstering the performance of cognitive radio systems.

articleTitle: IoT Security: Trends, Challenges, and Solutions for MQTT-Based Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Optimization and Applications (ICOA)
abstract: Incorporating the Internet of Things (IoT) into our society has gained significant technological momentum. This important progress has enabled seamless changes in corporate operations and services. However, the widespread use of this tech-nology also poses a significant security threat, which has become a top worry for many enterprises across the globe. This study highlights the key vulnerabilities in the MQ Telemetry Transport (MQTT) protocol used in IoT devices, including exposure to DDoS attacks, compromising service availability, and Man-in-the-Middle (MITM) attacks exploiting plaintext transmission of credentials, risking data confidentiality. Additionally, it discusses information disclosure vulnerabilities, inadequate authentication, and identity spoofing as further risks. These findings emphasize the importance of vigorous security measures, such as encryption and strong access control, to protect MQTT-based IoT devices.

articleTitle: Comparison of Generative AI Models in Supply Chain Management: Benefits, Applications and Challenges
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Optimization and Applications (ICOA)
abstract: This paper explores the utilization of three prominent AI techniques—Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), (VAEs), and Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs)—in SCM. The review provides insights into the application areas, benefits, challenges, and future directions of these AI techniques in optimizing different segments of the supply chain.

articleTitle: Early Prediction Model for Anemia in Infants Using Clinical Data from Perú Applying Supervised Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Optimization and Applications (ICOA)
abstract: Anemia is a disease that is always present from early stages; children are the most prone to contracting it from birth if it's not diagnosed, which can lead to more severe illnesses. Therefore, a predictive model is proposed for the detection of anemia in infants using their clinical data. The Cross Industry Standard Process for Data Mining (CRISP-DM) methodology is employed, along with Analysis Services for the Extract, Transform, Load (ETL) process and four Machine Learning (ML) algorithms: Logistic Regression (LR), Decision Tree (DT), Support Vector Machine (SVM), and Random Forest (RF). All four phases of CRISP-DM were utilized: Business Understanding, Data Understanding, Data Preparation, Modeling, and Evaluation. The dataset used consists of 400,000 records related to the medical history of children from a healthcare institution in Peru, from which 27 variables were selected. The results showed that the DT algorithm performed better, achieving an AUC-ROC Curve greater than 93%, and the “Scikit Learn” library for ML in Python facilitated obtaining the results.

articleTitle: Weaving Sustainability Strategies in Supply Chain: A Carbon Trading Perspective
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Optimization and Applications (ICOA)
abstract: Addressing the evolving landscape of sustainable supply chains to integrate innovations in carbon trading is crucial for the MENA region. With rapid industrialization and economic growth hitting this region, environmental pressures are keeping pace. In this regard, though carbon trading schemes are a writ-large factor for mitigating climate change, strategic adaptation within pre-existing supply chains will be required if they are implemented. The challenge must be addressed not just to reduce carbon footprints but also to have lasting economic resilience with environmental sustainability in a region nearing very substantive sustainable development. This paper highlighted some of the critical factors associated with carbon trading and employed the Best-Worst method to rank, in order of importance, those factors. The results show Geopolitical considerations relatively high, at 0.218 for OC6, in understanding complex political dynamics that might prevail and impact strategic effectiveness. Finally, specific technical preconditions are required if carbon trading processes are to avoid failure and be reliable: data management and transparency ranked 0.249 (TC1) and the need for solid technology infrastructure, ranked highest at 0.270 (TC2).

articleTitle: Improving Road Accident Severity Classification with Cluster-Based Severity Resampling: A Hybrid Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Optimization and Applications (ICOA)
abstract: In response to the rising number of vehicles and corresponding increase in road accidents within urban environments, this study introduces a hybrid approach that combines clustering and classification of road accident severity to aid city planning and enhance public safety in smart cities. To address the imbalance in real-world accident data, which particularly affects the accurate prediction of fatal accidents often underrepresented in datasets, we employed clustering as a foundational structure for data segmentation. We developed a method based on two clusters for severity resampling. Within each cluster, we applied targeted resampling techniques, enhanced by SMOTE and ADASYN, to achieve a balanced representation of severity classes. Our comparative analysis reveals that our approach significantly outperforms models trained on both the original imbalanced dataset and those modified by standard resampling techniques. Specifically, we observed an increase in G-mean from 0.02 and 0.29 to 0.70 and an improvement in AUC-ROC by 35%, and 38% respectively. These enhancements highlight the efficacy of integrating clustering techniques into accident severity classification. This robust and adaptable methodology consistently improves predictions of accident severity in urban environments, demonstrating its effectiveness across various methodological setups.

articleTitle: Challenges in Medical Image Segmentation: Insights from Transformer-CNN Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Optimization and Applications (ICOA)
abstract: After the success of Transformers in the field of computer vision, via the VIT architecture, several hybrid approaches have emerged combining Transformers and CNN to leverage the strengths of both. This hybrid architecture marks a significant advance in medical diagnostics, with numerous research projects highlighting its potential to improve diagnostic accuracy thereby enhancing patient care outcomes. The primary aim of this paper is to present these advances by focusing on the segmentation of medical images, we provide the fundamentals of transformer-based architectures and we will present the different ways to combine transforms with CNNs while showing the importance of each. In addition, we categorize the various challenges faced by this type of architecture and present the specific architectures that address each issue. This paper distinguishes itself from other reviews by specifically focusing on the integration methods of transformers for segmentation tasks, encompassing both spatial and frequency domains. In conclusion, we highlight the major challenges and explore various potential directions for future research.

articleTitle: Generative Adversarial Networks in ECG Signal Denoising: A Survey
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Optimization and Applications (ICOA)
abstract: In this survey, we present a thorough analysis of denoising ECG signal approaches using Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs). Our aim with this survey is to examine the most recent studies that have utilized different types of GANs architecture for removing various types of noise from ECG signals, ranging from real-world to synthetic noise. This review paper offers experts a clear understanding of ECG denoising methods, particularly those utilizing the GANs architecture, and enables them to explore unresolved issues. We have identified several limitations and recognized the need for improvement to enhance the performance of these approaches in handling different types of noise with varying SNR levels, while also minimizing preprocessing and computational costs. Ultimately, our intention is to address the raised concerns and limitations to further enhance the performance of ECG signal denoising approaches, especially those utilizing GAN architecture, thereby increasing their potential for practical clinical diagnosis.

articleTitle: Enhancing Identity Security in the Metaverse: Solutions Using AI, Blockchain, and NFTs
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Optimization and Applications (ICOA)
abstract: As the metaverse evolves into an all-encompassing digital ecosystem, ensuring the security and uniqueness of digital identities and assets becomes paramount. This paper critically examines the identity security challenges in the metaverse, particularly focusing on the unicity problem. We propose an integrated solution leveraging the synergistic capabilities of Artificial Intelligence (AI), blockchain technology, and Non-Fungible Tokens (NFTs). Our novel contribution lies in the multifaceted approach that combines AI for sophisticated identity verification and anomaly detection, blockchain for decentralized and immutable record-keeping, and NFTs for establishing verifiable ownership and authenticity of digital assets. This robust framework addresses the pressing need for enhanced security measures in the metaverse, not only mitigating current security risks but also paving the way for future advancements in digital identity management. Our comprehensive analysis and proposed methodology provide a significant contribution to the ongoing discourse on metaverse security, highlighting both the potential and challenges of integrating these emerging technologies. This paper serves as a foundational work for future research and development in the secure management of digital identities and assets within the metaverse.

articleTitle: Optimal Scheduling of Programmable Appliances for Demand Management in Energy Communities
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Optimization and Applications (ICOA)
abstract: Increasing the share of Renewable Energy Sources (RES) in energy consumption is perceived today as essential to decarbonizing energy systems. In this context, the Renewable Energy Communities (RECs) have been recently introduced to create a more decentralized energy system, where each member may share RES-based energy production to increase local self-consumption. To maximize the benefits for each member, the RES-based energy generation should match the demand. Thus, demand management may contribute in this regard by introducing load-shifting for the electric appliances used by REC's members. In this view, different modeling approaches are proposed as Mixed Integer Linear Programming and Mixed Integer Quadratic Programming. Solutions can be used to suggest possible changes to the end-users' current habits. Simulations are performed to compare energy, economic, and environmental Key Performance Indicators, including self-consumption, self-sufficiency, and CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emission savings.

articleTitle: Quality Process Control and Preventive Maintenance Optimization of a Grinding Unit: A Case Study
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Optimization and Applications (ICOA)
abstract: The studied process is a grinding and hydroclassification unit designed to ensure that the grain size it processes is in line with the specifications for the pipe's transport mode. Obstacles to the unit's operational process include frequent stops, plant's low reliability, product delivery with an inappropriate grain size, and a lack of control over operating parameters. These factors have a significant impact on the unit's relevance and, consequently, its performance. We created a quality culture among operators with “0 grain quality loss” through the implementation of the quality and processes control study, which was essential to improve the situation. Thus, by completing the seven project stages, we were able to enhance and optimize the grinding and hydroclassification unit's overall performance and capability to regulate the grain size quality. We noticed a notable improvement in regulating the several parameters that affect the targeted particle size after we established tools for unit quality control, such as control and monitoring charts, reaction matrices, intervention flow charts and operational standards. The unit has seen a great deal of satisfaction from the project in terms of quality, process control and resources optimization. Moreover, the incorporation of preventive maintenance into this process has shown to be crucial in guaranteeing the reliability and durability of the installation, thereby substantially improving the unit's overall efficiency.

articleTitle: Analyzing the Dynamics of Nelson-Siegel-Svensson Term Structure Models Using Time Series Data*
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Optimization and Applications (ICOA)
abstract: The aim of this study is to analyze the specific dynamics of the term structure of interest rates. The methodology used to construct the yield curve is based on the Nelson-Siegel-Svensson model. Latent factors influence the term structure of interest rates based on several parameters (levels, slopes, and curvatures) that evolve over time in a deterministic manner. To better model the temporal structure of different maturities, principal component analysis is used to identify the factors responsible for variations in the observed realizations of the yield curve. Once the aggregate curve is constructed, a non-stationarity analysis is applied to identify the generating process and the specific dynamics of the term structure of interest rates. The results indicate that the Moroccan bond market follows a random walk without drift. This provides a first indication of the efficiency of this market since 2004.

articleTitle: Analysis of Public Debt Management Practices in Low- and Middle-Income Countries: Intensity and Use of Academic Research
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Optimization and Applications (ICOA)
abstract: Public debt management presents significant challenges for low- and middle-income countries, requiring effective and well-informed strategies. Academic research can play a crucial role in providing valuable analysis and recommendations. This study focuses on assessing how academic research is utilized by debt management offices (DMOs) in these countries to manage public debt. Through a survey, we aim to uncover the extent to which DMOs integrate academic insights into their practices, identifying both effective approaches and challenges encountered. This examination aims to improve our understanding of these processes, thereby improving public debt management and strengthening the link between academic research and public policy, particularly from the perspective of DMOs. The results of the survey indicate that, although the importance of academic research is recognized, its practical application in debt management strategies remains limited due to various barriers and the restricted collaboration between academia and DMOs. Furthermore, from the perspective of the DMOs, this study suggests ways to enhance interactions between DMOs and academic institutions, including through workshops, joint conferences, and research partnerships focused on topics of mutual interest.

articleTitle: Towards the Design of Maturity Model for Digital Supply Chain in Automotive Industry
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Optimization and Applications (ICOA)
abstract: The automotive industry is currently undergoing a profound transformation through digitalization, where advanced technologies are reshaping traditional processes and fostering innovation. This evolution extends beyond the design and production of vehicles, encompassing the entire supply chain. Digitalization plays a crucial role in revolutionizing manufacturing processes, introducing features like smart manufacturing, connected vehicles, data analytics, and artificial intelligence. The integration of digital technologies into the automotive supply chain enhances efficiency, reduces costs, and facilitates seamless collaboration among stakeholders. Therefore, this study seeks to initiate the development of a maturity model for digital supply chains within the automotive industry. As a result, an initial draft of the “Digital Supply Chain Maturity Model” (DSCMM) is introduced. Maturity levels and their corresponding characteristics are identified and detailed. The topic area is organized into ten dimensions. Although the model requires further refinement and extensive evaluation, this preliminary research can encourage future investigations and provide a robust foundation for the model's ongoing development.

articleTitle: Fit-for-Purpose: Analysis of Occupancy Behaviour Impacts on Intelligent Control Performances in a Nearly Zero Energy Building
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Optimization and Applications (ICOA)
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to evaluate how different occupancies' conditions affect the performance of building controllers. The study focuses on a nearly zero energy large commercial building with various systems such as boilers, chillers, a building-integrated photovoltaic system, and a combined cooling, heating, and power unit. The building management system incorporates a supervisory genetic algorithm optimization, mid-range controller, and internal controller of equipment using a cascade approach. The mid-range controller is designed using three approaches: 1) proportional-integral-derivative controller tuned by a fuzzy logic system, 2) model predictive controller, and 3) an optimized traditional relay controller. The impacts of occupancies on the controllers are assessed through one factor at a time sensitivity analysis of occupancy density, occupancy activity, and setpoints. The study found that the model predictive controller improved energy efficiency by varying percentages (7% to 85<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>) based on occupancy uncertainty, while maintaining a robust thermal comfort performance of around 95% accuracy during different conditions. The PID-fuzzy controller tunes the energy resources to improve energy performance of the building by 15% in accurate modelling, the robustness of its performances in the presence of occupational uncertainty resulting in reducing the impact of occupancies to 5% energy performance gap.
